scope: Evaluate whether AN and EN can be governed as a narrowly scoped first-person / second-person referential pair without creating a full pronoun paradigm, subject grammar, possessive grammar, agreement or person-number morphology.

AN.observation: AN occurs in the position compatible with the speaker/self referent.
AN repeats in a declarative language-use frame structurally parallel to PHR-002.

EN.observation: EN is compatible with the addressee/second-person referent.
EN repeats in an interrogative-like addressee position.
EN repeats in an interrogative-like addressee position.
EN repeats before the language-use predicate in an interrogative frame.

EN.phrase: KALA YA EN ES KU KE
EN.observation: EN occurs inside a name-question frame whose translation contains second-person possession, but the exact internal syntactic contribution of EN is not independently recovered.

existing_authored_mappings.AN: AUTH-016: first-person referent / I for scoped beginner use; CLOSED_LIST_ONLY
existing_authored_mappings.EN: AUTH-017: second-person referent / you for scoped beginner use; CLOSED_LIST_ONLY

findings: AN has repeated distribution compatible with a first-person speaker/self referent.
EN has repeated distribution compatible with a second-person addressee referent.
The corpus does not recover a full person/number paradigm.
The corpus does not establish subject versus object case, possessive morphology, agreement, gender, plural, politeness or clusivity.
PHR-001 does not by itself prove that EN is a possessive pronoun; translation-level possession must not be projected into HNK syntax.
Existing AUTH-016/AUTH-017 already govern narrow person-reference mappings, so B14 can clarify scope without promoting lexical authority.

options.label: SCOPED_PERSON_REFERENT_PAIR_NO_PARADIGM
options.effect: Govern AN as first-person speaker/self referent and EN as second-person addressee referent in already-scoped beginner/attested domains. Do not define them as a complete pronoun paradigm or assign subject/possessive/case behavior outside separately governed constructions.

options.label: PROMOTE_TO_GENERAL_PRONOUN_PARADIGM
options.risk: Would overgeneralize from a small phrase corpus and incorrectly infer subject/possessive/case behavior.

options.label: KEEP_PERSON_REFERENCE_ENTIRELY_UNRESOLVED
options.risk: Would discard repeated distribution plus already-governed AUTH-016/AUTH-017 mappings without new contrary evidence.

boundaries: No grammatical subject category assigned by B14.
No possessive grammar assigned to EN from PHR-001.
No singular/plural morphology beyond the narrow person-reference interpretation.
No gender, politeness, clusivity, agreement or pro-drop rules.
No general clause order; B16 owns that question.
No interrogative architecture; B15 owns KU/KE/KUVAN/KUON.
